content: Emtricitabine, marketed under the brand name EMTRIVA, is a synthetic nucleoside analog that exhibits activity against the reverse transcriptase enzyme of human immunodeficiency virus type 1 (HIV-1). The chemical name of emtricitabine is 5-fluoro-1-(2R,5S)-cytosine. Structurally, it is the enantiomer of a thio analog of cytidine, distinguished from other cytidine analogs by the presence of a fluorine atom at the 5-position. The molecular formula of emtricitabine is C8H10FN3O3S, and its molecular weight is 247.24 g/mol. It appears as a white to off-white powder and has a solubility of approximately 112 mg/mL in water at 25°C. The compound has a log P value of -0.43, indicating its hydrophilic nature, and a pKa of 2.65. EMTRIVA is available in two formulations: capsules and an oral solution. The capsules are intended for oral administration, with each capsule containing 200 mg of emtricitabine. The inactive ingredients in the capsules include crospovidone, magnesium stearate, microcrystalline cellulose, povidone, titanium dioxide, gelatin, and FD&C Blue No. 2. The oral solution is also designed for oral administration, with each milliliter (1 mL) containing 10 mg of emtricitabine in an aqueous solution. The inactive components of the oral solution include cotton candy flavor, FD&C Yellow No. 6, edetate disodium, methylparaben, and propylparaben (used as preservatives), sodium phosphate (monobasic), propylene glycol, water, and xylitol (used as a sweetener). Additionally, sodium hydroxide and hydrochloric acid may be utilized to adjust the pH of the solution.
